label: E. coli
plain: A rod-shaped bacterium of the animal gut: 4,403 proteins in UniProt's reference proteome of strain K-12, in a cell a few micrometres long with two membranes and a wall between them. It swims with flagella.

modelled.text: The project's record adds it as a data-only organism, for a proposed track whose first stage is bacterial chemotaxis in a well-mixed cell; the track is on hold (decision D179, 15 November 2026). Nothing of it is in the engine: no organism definition, no model and no run.

record.where: D179: The FEP track's decisions: on hold, E. coli as data only

levels.label: One cell
levels.note: Drawn as a rod 2.5 µm long and 1 µm across: the picture's choice, within the ranges given for the cell. Its second membrane and its wall are drawn as clear shells around the cell membrane, and its 6,800 ribosomes are the low end of the range one paper gives. Its flagella and fimbriae are given as appendages, with the ranges their sources give; that the fimbriae stand all over the cell is the picture's choice, since no source read for this file says where they stand.

no_further_levels: A single-celled organism: each cell lives on its own, so there is no tissue, organ or body.

facts.label: Shape and size
facts.value: a straight rod; earlier work put its average length between 1.6 and 3.1 µm and its width at 0.7 to 1.1 µm, and one study measured 1.6 µm (cells at rest) to 3.9 µm (cells growing on a rich medium) in length and 1.26 µm in width

facts.label: Volume
facts.value: 1.5 to 4.4 femtolitres, by the conditions it grows in

facts.label: Envelope
facts.value: two membranes: the inner one separates the cytoplasm from the periplasm, the outer one the periplasm from the cell's surroundings; the cell wall lies between them

facts.label: Inside
facts.value: a bacterium, with no nucleus: its chromosome lies in a region of the cytoplasm that no membrane surrounds

facts.label: Proteins
facts.value: 4,403 in UniProt's reference proteome of strain K-12, every one with a reviewed entry

facts.label: Ribosomes
facts.value: between 6,800 and 72,000 in a cell, depending on its phase of growth, as one open paper sums up earlier estimates

facts.label: Movement
facts.value: swims with flagella that grow all over its surface, or does not move

facts.label: Flagella
facts.value: 1 to 5 on a cell in one study of single cells, and 3.4 on average by another paper; each a thread typically 5 to 10 µm long (7.5 µm by one measurement). Of the width the sources disagree: about 20 nm by one, 40 nm by another

facts.label: Where the flagella stand
facts.value: all over the cell body; the motor at the foot of each sits in the inner membrane, where its ring protein FliF and its stator proteins MotA and MotB are stated to be. 34 proteins are parts of the flagellum by the Gene Ontology terms UniProt gives them

facts.label: Type 1 fimbriae
facts.value: 200 to 500 on a cell by one paper's summary, each up to 1 µm long and about 7 to 10 nm wide, standing out from the outer membrane

facts.label: Chemotaxis
facts.value: 22 of its proteins carry UniProt's keyword for chemotaxis (aer, cheA, cheB, cheR, cheW, cheY, cheZ, dppA, fliG, fliJ, fliL, fliM, fliN, fliO, mglB, motA, motB, rbsB, tap, tar, trg and tsr), and 34 are parts of the flagellum by the Gene Ontology terms UniProt gives them

facts.label: Energy
facts.value: respiration and fermentation: it lives with or without oxygen

facts.label: Where it lives
facts.value: the lower gut of animals; it survives when released to the natural environment

facts.label: Ion channels
facts.value: none of the animal families Cells has laws for; 15 proteins of bacterial channel families (aqpZ, clcA, clcB, corA, glpF, kch, mscK, mscL, mscM, mscS, ybdG, ybiO, yfeO, ynaI and zntB)

facts.label: Signalling
facts.value: 64 proteins carry UniProt's keyword for two-component regulatory systems

facts.label: Strain
facts.value: K-12; the genome record is of its substrain MG1655, and UniProt's proteome is of the same genome assembly (GCA_000005845.2)

cap.membrane.note: It has two membranes. By UniProt's vocabulary the inner one separates the cytoplasm from the periplasm, and the outer one the periplasm from the cell's surroundings. No source read for this file measured a voltage across either.

cap.channels.note: Not the channels of animal cells: none of its proteins carries the signature of a channel family that Cells has a law for. 15 of its proteins carry the signature of a bacterial channel family: the potassium channel domain (kch); the large-conductance mechanosensitive channel (MscL) (mscL); the mechanosensitive channel MscS (mscK, mscM, mscS, ybdG, ybiO and ynaI); chloride channels of the ClC family (clcA, clcB and yfeO); aquaporins and their relatives (major intrinsic proteins) (aqpZ and glpF); CorA-type magnesium channels (corA and zntB).

cap.pumps.note: Not the pumps of animal cells: none of its proteins carries the signature of the sodium-potassium pump. Its P-type ATPases (copA, kdpB, mgtA and zntA) and its ATP synthase are stated to be in the inner membrane.

cap.junctions.why: It lives as single cells and has no gap junctions: none of its proteins carries the signature of connexins or innexins.

cap.extracellular.note: Two spaces lie beyond its inner membrane: the periplasm, between its two membranes, and what surrounds the cell, the lower gut of an animal or wherever it is released.

cap.water.note: By UniProt's vocabulary a wall lies between its two membranes and plays a part in the cell's shape and stability. One of its proteins, AqpZ, carries the signature of the aquaporin family.

cap.calcium.why: It has no endoplasmic reticulum, the store this capability concerns: no entry of its proteome states a place in one, and none of its proteins carries the signature of the store's calcium pump or of its release channels.

cap.energy.note: It lives by respiration and by fermentation, with or without oxygen; its ATP synthase is stated to be in the inner membrane.

cap.mitochondria.why: It is a bacterium and has no mitochondria: no entry of its proteome states a place in one. Its ATP synthase is in the inner membrane.

cap.circuits.note: At the chromosome, which lies in a region of the cytoplasm that no membrane surrounds: there is no nucleus. 64 of its proteins carry UniProt's keyword for two-component regulatory systems.

cap.grn.why: It forms no tissue, so there is nothing for gene networks to be coupled across. Gene expression within the one cell belongs with regulatory circuits.

cap.trafficking.why: It has no endoplasmic reticulum and no Golgi: no entry of its proteome states a place in either. By the names of their entries, its proteins cross or enter the inner membrane through the Sec and Tat translocases.

cap.assembly.note: Its assemblies are its ribosomes, RNA polymerase, the ATP synthase, its flagella and its chemoreceptor arrays. The designed protein cage that Cells models is not one of its proteins.

cap.machines.note: Its ribosomes, RNA polymerase, the ATP synthase, the protein translocases and the motor of its flagella. One of its proteins carries the signature of the proteasome's subunits: its entry names it "ATP-dependent protease subunit HslV".

cap.secretion.note: Some of its proteins are stated to be secreted, and porins and transporters carry molecules across its two membranes. Signalling between its own cells was not looked for.

cap.repair.note: The place would be its envelope. No source read for this file describes an injury of it or its resealing in this organism.

cap.division.note: It divides as a single cell: its proteome names the cell division protein FtsZ.

cap.replacement.why: It forms no tissue, so there is no neighbour for a new cell to replace.

cap.mechanics.why: It forms no sheet: its cells share no edges to pull on. Its own movement, swimming with flagella, is not what this capability models.

cap.sheet.why: It lives as single cells and forms no sheet of coupled cells.
